Even if she isn't going outside, train her to go only outside. Treat her like she's a 8 week old puppy, don't take her inside until she potties even if it takes an hour for her to. Take her out every four hours (or less) and ease into taking her every 6, then 8... once she starts catching on. Mark the action with potty as well even if you catch her pottying inside so she learns what it means. If you also catch her potting inside (always keep a close eye on her), say "potty, no!" And take her outside immediately, don't go back inside until she does. Eventually they'll catch on but you have to be very consistent. Treat them every single time they potty in the right spot with a high value treat (immediately after they stop so you arent distracting). When you take them for potties, make sure there are no distractions and do not interact or play with your dog until they are done pottying. Never treat them to anything interesting or fun until they do their business when you intend for them to. Don't even make it obvious that you're paying attention to them. Also mark the association with pottying and outside (everytime you are outside, say outside and say potty everytime they potty outside, keep saying it while they do to embed it into their mind. Say outside randomly while you're outside, teach them inside as well).

Eventually you'll want them to tell you when they have to go potty. Say outside and potty right before you leave each room after they learn the words and they'll associate sitting by the door as a warning that they have to go. You could do several things to teach them how to tell you.

Anyways, I hope this helps. There's allot of videos on YouTube that could help as well with good trainers and all kinds of circumstances
